case_name: State of Himachal Pradesh v Wazir Chand and Others
facts: The occurrence which gave rise to the present appeals took place on August 7, 1972 a little after 10.30 p.m.
Parshottam Lal according to prosecution who was fatally injured in this occurrence had a few days prior to August 7, 1972 earned a prize in the amount of Rs. 5100 in a private lottery.
On the date of the occurrence deceased Parshottam Lal accompanied by one Om Prakash alias Pashi visited Jyoti Cinema in the second show.
Accused 1 Wazir Chand and Joginder Singh were seen conversing among themselves in the verandah of the theatre.

Deshraj PW 3 who was also enjoying the picture came out of the theatre and proceeded towards his house and on the way he crossed accused 3 Joginder Singh whose clothes appeared to have been stained with blood.
issues: Whether the charge against accused 2 and 3 is not brought home to them
Whether accused 1 Wazir Chand can be convicted for an offence under Section 304, Part ii of the Indian Penal Code, 1860
petitioner_arguments: The defence of accused 1 Wazir Chand was that he caused injury to Parshottam Lal in exercise of the right of private defence of body
The defence of accused 2 Raj Kumar and accused 3 Joginder Singh was one of total denial
court_reasoning: The learned Sessions Judge rejected the evidence of motive and he accepted the dying declaration as giving a truthful version of the occurrence
He also accepted the circumstantial evidence in the form of recovery of blood-stained knife, Ex. P-1 at the instance of accused 1 Wazir Chand
holding: The State of Himachal Pradesh has questioned the correctness of the judgment of the High Court in respect of the three accused
Accused 1 questioned the correctness of his conviction and sentence
The capital punishment awarded to accused 1 was set aside and he was awarded rigorous imprisonment for 10 years
cases_cited: State of Himachal Pradesh v Wazir Chand
